glossary.lung collapse: The lung shrinking away from the chest wall so it cannot inflate properly.
glossary.ipsilateral: On the same side as the problem.
glossary.percussion: Tapping on the chest to hear whether the area underneath is full of air, fluid or solid tissue.
glossary.air entry: How well air can be heard moving into the lung on listening with a stethoscope.
glossary.breath sounds: The sounds of air moving in the lungs heard through a stethoscope.
glossary.apical: At the top (apex) of the lung.
glossary.cannabis: A recreational drug; smoking it raises the risk of pneumothorax.
glossary.pulmonary fibrosis: Scarring and stiffening of the lung tissue.
glossary.aortic dissection: A tear in the inner wall of the aorta letting blood split its layers.
glossary.trauma: Physical injury, such as a stab wound or rib fracture.
glossary.chest expansion: How much the chest moves outward on breathing in.
glossary.haemodynamic instability: Unstable blood pressure and heart rate, with poor perfusion of organs.
glossary.distended neck veins: Visibly swollen neck veins from blood backing up when it cannot return to the heart.
glossary.lung markings: The fine lines of blood vessels seen on a chest X-ray throughout normal lung.
glossary.CT chest: A detailed cross-sectional X-ray scan of the chest.
glossary.water seal chamber: The part of a chest drain bottle under water that lets air out but not back in.
glossary.conservative management: Watching and supporting without an invasive procedure.
glossary.ambulatory device: A small portable drain with a valve that lets the patient go home with it in place.
glossary.18-gauge cannula: A medium-sized needle with a plastic sheath used for aspiration.
glossary.inpatient monitoring: Being kept in hospital to be observed.
glossary.outpatient follow-up: A clinic review after going home.
glossary.hypoxia: Too little oxygen reaching the tissues.
glossary.cardiothoracic surgery: The surgical specialty operating on the heart, lungs and chest.
glossary.thoracostomy: Making an opening into the chest cavity to let air or fluid out.
glossary.cardiac preload: The filling of the heart with blood before it contracts; falls when great veins are compressed.
glossary.recurrence: The condition coming back after treatment.
glossary.intrapleural pressure: The pressure in the pleural space, normally slightly negative to keep the lung inflated.
glossary.one-way valve: A flap letting air in on inspiration but not out on expiration.
glossary.mediastinum: The central compartment of the chest containing the heart, great vessels, trachea and oesophagus.
glossary.great veins: The large veins returning blood to the heart: the superior and inferior vena cava.
glossary.reperfusion injury: Tissue damage caused when blood and oxygen suddenly return to an area.
glossary.capillary permeability: How easily fluid leaks out through the walls of the smallest blood vessels.
glossary.pulmonary oedema: Fluid in the lung air spaces, causing breathlessness.
glossary.ICS: Intercostal space: the gap between two ribs.
